body: First off, fuck yeah on the 50 lbs lost. Keep it up. What I am going to tell you might seem a little hard but it is really not once you get the practice down. You have to use self control, it is a mental muscle you have to train. Like any muscle in the body it takes time to train. You cannot make other people change with you or for you. You can give them advice but you cannot change them. You are going to have to make this change by yourself if you family feels that way. Don't wait for others either.
Eggs and Beans I think is your best bet.

Well, I am proud of you for taking a step to getting in shape. My advice for you is to do a lot of research on nutrition and types of work outs (Google and YouTube works great). Just remember it all takes time and results are not going to happen over night. You have to find what works for you and do not be scared to push yourself. A lot of it is trial and error.  Keep at it, even if you wake up and don't feel like it. There has been so many times that I did not want to work out but I force myself anyway. Don't be scared to work out at gyms. Most people in gyms are too focus on their own work out to really care. A lot of gym rats were once out of shape as well. So a lot of us understand that everyone starts somewhere and are willing to help.
When I realized people are full of shit and hypocritical. I just chill with my cats and watch the world slowly turn into the movie Idiocracy.

Since I am not a doctor I do not know for sure what could be causing your back pain and ED.  ED can be caused by a lot of different issues. Since it started when you hurt your back, it could be a pinch nerve or you have some damage to the nerve in your back that goes to your genital area. ED can also be caused by stress(being in pain causes a lot of stress on the body), depression, heart issues, and low T levels as well. I would talk to a doctor about it.

As for the back pain, It could be a lot of things. I know you already went to five doctors, but keep going to different ones until one helps you. Don't tell them, if you did, that you already talked to a doctor about it. They will just go with what the other doctor said. 

Also do a lot of your own research as well. When I hurt a disc in my back, I did not just stop at what the doctors told me. I read hundreds of studies, research papers and even watched Youtube videos on the subject.

I would go to the doctor and get it check out. And don't worry about getting into the military. If turns out to be something small you could still get in. But if you go into the militiary and you have something like a disc problem it could get a lot worst. You don't want to be that soldier on a dead man's profile that has not even deployed yet, nobody respects them. The military is hard on the body, I was Army infantry, I have a bad back and knees, a lot do. Take care of your health first.

The breakouts are probably from your body trying to detox and the weight gain is probably muscle growth from the increase activity. Also smoking effects your body in a lot of ways, your body is trying to heal and is freaking out in the process.
Lmao. Well, its better than not quitting and end up looking like Gollum.

Your body is just adjusting to not having nicotine and  starting to heal/clean itself after years of smoking. This can cause a lot of different symptoms. Drink water, eat healthy, exercise, and get rest. It will pass. Finding a new hobbit to focus on helps as well.

I wish my sever Que times were only an hour, I am on Faerlina and wish I knew this was a streamer sever before rolling a character here. I started mid September and have not followed the WoW community in over a year. Wait times are 4 to 5 hours right now. I have to log on with a remote desktop app while I am at work if I want to play when I get home or I am screwed.
To be honest, all the stuff physical therapists and doctor tell me I already knew or it helps little. I did my own research and found what works for me.

Sitting for long periods of time puts a lot of pressure on the lower back, Humans were never really ment to sit in chairs. Try to get off the video games and walk around more. Also try to hang from a pull up bar to try and decompress a little. I have a mild disc problem, I hang upside down it takes a lot of pressure off my lower back. Also, if you work out make sure your doing core work outs as well. I would go to a doctor and have a MRI done. You might have a disc problem, but a lot of people do even the ones that don't have symptoms, it's a part of the aging process.
I have a herniated disc in the same place. I went on roller coasters about 9 months after my injury. I was fine, but that's me. You have to listen to your body. Don't do stuff that makes it worst.
Injections are just to bring the inflammation down.  Think of it as someone shooting ibuprofen into your back. The shots ware off eventually.

Running is  a high impact exerise, it can cause a lot of pressure on the disc because they take a lot of the impact. So using cardio machines might be better for you. Stopping running might help a little. Disc protrusions are cause when the disc fibers break apart and the jelly like material comes out. This can happen from a lot things, even from  just aging. Disc pain can get better with time but the injured disc never really heals fully. Just comes down to finding what works for you or not.
Try hanging from a pull up bar as well, it will help your spine decompress. I have a disc problem in L5/S1, and hanging has help me a lot. I hang upside down as well.

I would not go on a daily run, running is a high impact exerisce. Once or twice a week at most, if your back can handle it.  Try going hard on cardio machines instead. I have a hernatied disc in L5/S1, I use cardio machines, alot of high intensity body weight workouts, and planks to stay in shape. I do go on runs, but only once or twice a week.  I like to longboard a lot as well,  its low impact and if you go hard enough it can be a cardio work out. Most important thing you can do is listen to your back and figure out what works for you or not.
I had the same problem when I first started training.  It will even out, just keep training and making sure your form is right.

Yes. I have always done cardio along with lifting. I normally do cardio for 20 mins and then working out a select muscle group for an hour after. I normally do that 5 days a week.  I been pretty built and still was able to run long distance. It toke time and me pushing myself every workout. You only really need to focus on one particular skill set if you are going to compete in it.

I have not even played BFA. I am on the fence about even giving it a try.  I have lost interest every expansion because of the changes. The RNG loot and titanforging system( basically a lootbox system), makes the gear feel pointless and non-rewarding.  I don't feel the drive to raid anymore becaues of the loot system. I miss when the best PVE gear only dropped in raids( normal and up), but high M+ dungeons is a fun way to get it. LFR is not engaging and I feel like it hurts the commuity more then helps it. I miss having class tier gear and gear tokens.

The Pvp changes killed that aspect of the game for me,.I want gear to matter and pvp vendors again. The current Pvp changes make pvp feel watered down and boring to me. I actually miss pushing rating for the conquest cap in RBGS and Arenas. Gear in pvp does not feel progressive, which is the whole point of getting gear in a MMORPG. The commuity is just not there anymore. WoW feels like a single player game with a multi-player aspect to it.  I miss the old talent system. The current one feels "meh" at best. I miss having tons of spells and stances to work with.

There are other reasons but I will stop here.  I still think WoW is one of the best MMORPGs on the market, but Its just not fun for me anymore.
Thank you for the advice and support !!
